newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares soar at close on interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares soar at close on interest rate cut.

text.p: Chilean stocks surged to close up nearly four percent with the bolsa swept by jubilation over the Central Bank's long-awaited cut in interest rates, said traders.
But the bolsa could lose ground next week as players cash in gains from Friday's rally, said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
"There will doubtless be some profit-taking. The timing of the cut was unexpected," said Hurd.
The 40-share index ended up 3.81 percent at a year high of 115.89 points. The general index climbed 2.11 percent to 5,319.27 points.
Volume swelled to 19.6 billion pesos with strong buying from foreign investors, said traders.
"Funds have been underweight for so long that they are all trying to get back into the market," said one trader.

Investors were caught off guard by the rates cut as most were expecting the bank to wait until at least March after recent data showed higher-than-expected inflation in January and a sharp fall in unemployment in the last quarter of 1996.
"The bank choose the only week in which no-one expected a change in interest rates," said the trader.

The bank will continue to loosen its tight credit policy, which has been in force for over a year, provided that the economy meets growth and inflation targets, said bank head of research Nicolas Eyzaguirre.
Leading winners included power utility Enersis, up 5.86 percent at 271 pesos, telecom CTC, up 5.13 percent at 2,665 pesos and bottler Andina which rose 4.17 percent at 2,250 pesos.
There were just three losers including electricity firm Pehuenche, down 0.88 percent at 451 pesos and thread maker Cadena which slipped 0.62 percent to 80.5 pesos.
